message.content:
The drive from San Francisco to Los Angeles is roughly 380–400 miles (about 610–640 km) along the I‑5 corridor. Under normal conditions—no major traffic, construction, or weather delays—a typical car can cover that distance in about **6 hours**.  

If you’re heading out during peak commute times (especially around the Bay Area or the Los Angeles metro), you might add an extra hour or two for congestion, so plan for **7–8 hours** to be safe.  

A quick way to get a more precise estimate is to use a navigation app (Google Maps, Waze, Apple Maps) and enter your departure time; it will factor in real‑time traffic and give you a current ETA.
